citation: FET fusion oncoproteins impair ATM activation at double-strand breaks through their shared N-terminal IDR, leaving the ATR axis load-bearing.
what_it_supports: The synthetic-lethality premise the ATR route inherits, and the structural precondition (retain the N-terminal IDR, lose the C-terminal RGG repeats) that emc_fet_idr_census.py tests.

citation: Filion C et al. (2009) — the EWSR1::NR4A3 fusion transactivates a PPARG-promoter response element.
what_it_supports: That the fusion is a functional transcriptional driver acting through its DNA-binding domain; the fusion→PPARG axis both PPARG routes rest on; the DBD filter in fusion_object_inventory.py. ⚠ IT SUPPORTS THE AXIS, NOT A DIRECTION. The paper's own discussion proposes PPARγ AGONISTS; it has been cited in this repository for the OPPOSITE (an agonist-redundancy argument) and must not be again. One home: research/manuscripts/repurposing/pparg-direction-emc.md §3.
misattributed_as: the source of the agonist-redundancy argument

citation: "The most common fusion transcript contains exon 12 of EWSR1 fused to exon 3 of NR4A3 (type 1), whereas exon 7 of EWSR1 is fused to exon 2 of NR4A3 in the type 2 fusion transcript."
what_it_supports: The exon-level definitions of EWSR1::NR4A3 type 1 and type 2, and of TAF15::NR4A3.

citation: Agaram NP et al. (2014) — RT-PCR primer design: an EWSR1 exon 12 forward primer with an NR4A3 exon 3 reverse for type 1; an EWSR1 exon 7 forward with an NR4A3 exon 2 reverse for type 2.
what_it_supports: Independent corroboration of the type 1 and type 2 exon-level junctions.

what_it_supports: The type 5 junction; the TAF15::NR4A3 exclusivity; the TCF12::NR4A3 genomic-only breakpoint.

citation: A counted series: 10 of 15 EWS/CHN tumours were exon 12 :: exon 3; 2 of 15 were type 5.
what_it_supports: That type 1 is the commonest reported EWSR1::NR4A3 junction, on a counted series rather than an assertion.

citation: "E-N, corresponding to EWSR1 (exons 1-12)-NR4A3 (exons 3-8)"; "T-N*, corresponding to the commonest TAF15 (exons 1-6)-NR4A3 (exons 3-8) fusion"; and a rarer T-N isoform splicing into a cryptic exon in NR4A3 intron 2, "thus encoding 25 additional amino acids prior to the NR4A3 ATG".
what_it_supports: Expressed constructs corroborating type 1 and TAF15::NR4A3; the registered-but-deliberately-unmodelled cryptic-exon TAF15 isoform.

citation: EB-TCIP on EWSR1::FLI1, JACS 2025 — bivalent transcriptional chemically-induced proximity that co-opts a fusion TF.
what_it_supports: The TCIP route's mechanism and its stated first limitation — "Due to the dearth of EWSR1::FLI1-specific ligands, we have used a N-FKBP12^F36V-EWSR1::FLI1 model system" — which is what gives the route its W1 and also names its gap.

citation: Pioglitazone + trabectedin induced adipocyte differentiation and overcame trabectedin resistance in myxoid liposarcoma. Clin Cancer Res 2019;25:7565.
what_it_supports: That the combination already worked in the sibling myxoid sarcoma — the class-extension interest that gives the trabectedin+PPARγ route its taker.

citation: Bangerter et al. 2023, Hum Cell — ex-vivo drug sensitivity in patient-derived EMC models USZ20-EMC1 and USZ22-EMC2.
what_it_supports: The carfilzomib route's only ex-vivo EMC evidence. ⛔ READ THE SCOPE: the 40-drug panel (17 chemotherapies + 23 targeted agents) was screened on USZ20-EMC1 ALONE; carfilzomib was the only compound showing high sensitivity there, and carfilzomib/doxorubicin/venetoclax were then validated in BOTH models. Venetoclax showed NO monotherapy response and earns its place through additive/synergistic combination effects only.

citation: Maki RG, Kraft AS, Scheu K, Yamada J, Wadler S, Antonescu CR, Wright JJ, Schwartz GK. A multicenter Phase II study of bortezomib in recurrent or metastatic sarcomas. Cancer 2005;103(7):1431-8. PMID 15739208 · doi 10.1002/cncr.20968.
what_it_supports: ⛔ IT DOES NOT SUPPORT RT-CARFILZOMIB — IT BOUNDS IT, and it is the only human read on proteasome inhibition in the parent histology this repository holds. Two arms, Simon two-stage: arm A osteogenic sarcoma, Ewing sarcoma and rhabdomyosarcoma; arm B other soft tissue sarcomas. One confirmed partial response among 21 evaluable patients in arm B, in a patient with leiomyosarcoma; closed after the first stage of accrual; stated conclusion that bortezomib has minimal activity in soft tissue sarcoma AS A SINGLE AGENT and should be studied further in sarcoma only in combination with agents showing demonstrated preclinical synergy. ⚠ SCOPE: bortezomib, not carfilzomib; monotherapy; NOT EMC data, so it moves BLK-NO-EMC-DATA not at all. Whether any EMC patient was enrolled in arm B is UNREAD — abstract only.

citation: Boklan J, Langevin AM, Bielamowicz K, Neville K, Trippett T, Brown V, DuBois SG, Eshun F, Gelfond J, Zomet A, Narendran A, Lacayo NJ. A Phase I Study of Carfilzomib with Cyclophosphamide and Etoposide in Relapsed and Refractory Leukemia and Solid Tumors. Cancers (Basel) 2025;17(17):2924. PMID 40941020 · PMC12428389 · doi 10.3390/cancers17172924.
what_it_supports: The only record found in which carfilzomib ITSELF has been given to sarcoma patients: a dose-escalation of carfilzomib with cyclophosphamide and etoposide in relapsed or refractory leukaemia (stratum A, n=14) and non-CNS solid tumours (stratum B, n=24), aged 6 months to under 30 years. No maximum tolerated dose was reached in stratum B and a recommended phase 2 dose is reported. ⛔ IT IS A DOSE-FINDING STUDY AND NOT AN EFFICACY RESULT: the abstract reports no response rate, no comparator and no sarcoma denominator, and PubMed types the record `Journal Article`. Its closing sentence, quoted rather than paraphrased, is "Patients with sarcomas benefited most, warranting further evaluation". ⚠ NOT EMC data, and its partner drugs are cyclophosphamide and etoposide rather than the anthracycline the ex-vivo EMC screen pairs carfilzomib with.
provenance_flag: RETRIEVED 2026-08-28 from PubMed through the PubMed MCP connector; queries and verbatim abstract quotations in research/literature/carfilzomib-class-clinical-2026-08-28.json. ⚠ ABSTRACT ONLY — PMC12428389 exists and was NOT fetched, so any per-histology outcome table it may carry is unread.

citation: Palmerini E, Sanfilippo R, Grignani G, Buonadonna A, Romanini A, Badalamenti G, Ferraresi V, Vincenzi B, Comandone A, Pizzolorusso A, Brunello A, Gelsomino F, De Pas T, Ibrahim T, Gurrieri L, Grosso F, Zanelli F, Pantaleo MA, Milesi L, Ciuffreda L, Ferrari V, Marchesi E, Quattrini I, Righi A, Setola E, Carretta E, Casali PG, Picci P, Ferrari S. Transcription regulators and ultra-rare and other rare translocation-related sarcomas treated with trabectedin: A proof of principle from a post-hoc analysis. Front Oncol 2022;12:1042479. PMID 36568164 · PMC9780071 · doi 10.3389/fonc.2022.1042479.
what_it_supports: ⭐ THE SECOND EMC-SPECIFIC TRABECTEDIN RESPONSE DENOMINATOR THAT EXISTS, and the only one carrying an EMC patient with progressive disease on the drug. A post-hoc case series of the ultra-rare and other rare translocation-related sarcoma patients inside TrObs, the Italian Sarcoma Group's non-interventional retrospective study of trabectedin in routine practice (NCT02793050; 512 anthracycline-pretreated patients, 20 Italian sites, enrolled 2010-2015). Of the 36 patients, three had EMC, and Table 2's EMC row reads 0 objective responses, 2 stable disease, 1 progressive disease — disease control 2 of 3. ⛔ IT IS NOT A BETTER CASE FOR THE DRUG: it enlarges the EMC denominator on which the objective-response count for trabectedin is still ZERO. ⚠ SCOPE, FOUR PARTS. (1) NO EMC-SPECIFIC PFS OR OS IS REPORTED — Table 3 breaks PFS out by histology only for the three histologies that produced a response, and EMC is not among them; that is an absence in the paper, not an absence of the reading. (2) Response was assessed by the TREATING PHYSICIAN per RECIST 1.1, not by central radiology review, which is the opposite of EV-MORIOKA's basis. (3) Retrospective and non-interventional. (4) ⛔ POPULATION OVERLAP WITH chiusole2020's 'second line ... trabectedin 66% of 3' IS UNRESOLVED and this record is therefore CONTEXT rather than pooled evidence — same n, same 2-of-3 disease control, an overlapping enrolment window, and one author in common at Istituto Oncologico Veneto. No efficacy, safety, eligibility or clinical-readiness claim is made for EMC.
